title: Calculate Salary After a 10% Bonus
description:
The company is giving every employee a **10% bonus**. Calculate what each employee's new salary will be.

**Table: employees** — `id`, `name`, `department`, `salary`

Return `name`, `salary`, and `salary * 1.10` rounded to 2 decimal places, aliased as `salary_with_bonus`. Order by `name`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INT, name VARCHAR, department VARCHAR, salary DECIMAL(10,2)); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Alice','Engineering',90000.00),(2,'Bob','Engineering',85000.00),(3,'Carol','Sales',70000.00),(4,'Dave','Sales',65000.00),(5,'Eve','Marketing',75000.00),(6,'Frank','HR',60000.00);
solution_sql: SELECT name, salary, ROUND(salary * 1.10, 2) AS salary_with_bonus FROM employees ORDER BY name

test_cases.description: All 6 employees returned with salary_with_bonus column

hints: Multiply salary by 1.10 to add 10%. Alternatively use salary + salary * 0.10.
Wrap with ROUND(..., 2) to keep two decimal places.
explanation: salary * 1.10 multiplies each row's salary by 1.1 (equivalent to adding 10%). ROUND(..., 2) ensures the result has exactly two decimal places. Alice's salary 90000 × 1.10 = 99000.00, and so on for all 6 employees.
